utterances.text: Listen, I'm not God to say, Now it's going to rain, now it's going to be a clear sky. And you're not God either. And I don't want to pretend that I'm son of God either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in the river you saw some dead bodies above Jelah. You saw eight dead bodies. Jelah is a bit further from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes, on the hilltop above Jelah. And those bodies were later found. They were discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the 15th onwards, until the 26th of July or even the 3rd of August, you hid in the woods, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: I arrived Zepa on the 29th of July. Zepa fell. I was there seven days. I knew the area pretty well. From Bijeli Voda to Vratar, I knew the area very well. I returned again to Srebrenica, and until the 9th of September, I was hiding in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you also visited your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes, I visited all the villages. I was looking for food because I didn't have any food to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you went into the direction of Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes, then we decided to go in the direction of Kladanj because there was no food left in our villages, and some ten of us started walking. One stayed behind in Zutica. There was nine of us. We didn't know the road. We were wandering around like bovine. We started on the 9th, and on the 18th we arrived in Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karadzic, wrap up your cross-examination. Your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While you were hiding in the woods, while you were visiting Zepa and when you were walking from Zepa to Kladanj, did you encounter any Serbs, either civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes. In the forest whose name I don't know, we hit an ambush, but they didn't show us. They were patrolling a hilltop and they passed by us. We crossed that hill. We came to a brook and we saw two dead bodies in the brook. And from there, when we arrived at another hilltop, we didn't know where we were. And we saw smoke coming out from some bunkers. And then it started raining again. We hid ourselves in a cave. It was already dusk. We could hear them felling trees and making fire in the bunkers. We decided to go through there, between two bunkers. We came to a macadam road and we followed that road, and then we spotted a torch-light in a bunker and one of our party stepped on a branch. That branch broke and cracked, resembling the sound of a pistol, and they opened fire at us from that bunker. We managed to squeeze past the bunkers and we waited for day to break, and then we started walking down a steep slope. We heard bursts of fire and individual bullets. There was obviously a separation line there. We returned to the hilltop and then I looked at another hilltop and I saw some trees there, and I thought maybe this could be a village. We started walking towards that village, and we -- we could -- we walked through that forest and we arrived at a brook. And on the birch tree it says "Huso," that was carved in the tree. And there was an arrow. So we followed that arrow. Although we suspected that this might -- may have been a trap. And then we came to another brook and we suspected that there was somebody there. We returned from that brook, some 10 to 12 metres into -- into an area where we saw a bunker very close by. We saw smoke, and that's where we were sitting for some time. And then all of a sudden, we heard somebody shouting, Huso come here. And then one of us jumped and said, If are you a Muslim, come here. And he said, I am from Srebrenica. He came to us. He was a soldier but did not have a uniform, and we asked him where he was from and he said he was from Vlasenica and that his name was Meho. And then I asked him, If you are from Vlasenica, do you know Salko Redzic? And he said that was a very close neighbour and a close relative. I asked, Do you know anything about Salko? And he said Salko got killed. We came to their bunker. They give us coffee, they gave us lunch, and then from there they took us to a place called Taric [phoen], near Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that was a Muslim bunker?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes, that was a Muslim bunker. And they asked where we had crossed and we told him that we had crossed on the hilltop, and he told us that that hilltop was called Sokolina. I had not known that before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. I have no more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I do, and it's quite brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, earlier, starting at about page 38 of the transcript, there was a discussion of a statement that you gave in October 1995. We don't need to bring the statement up again. I'm just going to read the quote again that we talked about. It's written: "I heard that was an agricultural warehouse. The building was big with a yellow facade with a porter's lodge on the left of the entrance to the warehouse. The building was completely empty inside, and when we went inside we had to sit on the concrete floor." Witness, is it possible that what was meant here from your interview was that the warehouse was completely empty of equipment but, nonetheless, was full of people?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is too much.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I can strike that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was full of people and there was no equipment at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, when you went inside, do you remember seeing any equipment, or vehicles, or items?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Where I entered, there was not just one warehouse, there were several warehouses. There was no equipment there at all. Just people.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Can we have P0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, if you wish we can receive this document, this statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, Excellency. I would like to tender this statement and you can't see in that statement that he was a soldier. He somehow kept quiet about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's unnecessary part. We will receive 1D5577. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2255, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May we now have P4270.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I intervene, please, 1D5577. Two 5s, two 7s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, earlier today, beginning at page 32, there was a discussion about ammunition belts and your observations of seeing people with ammunition belts while you were in the area of the meadow and the road. Do you see the photo in front of you, the one that is indicated A, the one on the left-hand side? Sir, can you see a photo in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I don't -- I'm not asking you about these people in the photo, but on it, the man on the right-hand side, we see what appears to be an -- ammunition belts criss-crossing his chest. Does this look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: I don't know him. I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: That's fine. I'm not interested in who they are. What I'm interested in is what's on his body.

utterances.speaker: KDZ071
utterances.text: I can't tell you that I know them. I don't. I don't know them. And it was not me who put those ammunition belts on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I have nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wouldn't it be fair to ask if this is an ammunition for an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In those ammunition belts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what these are for. I never had an automatic rifle. I know what I had. I had my hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless my colleagues have questions for you, sir, this concludes your evidence as the last witness for the Prosecution in this case. And, on behalf of the Chamber and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague yet again to give it. Now you're free to go. Shall we excuse -- if you could excuse yourself. Yes, we'll draw the blind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a couple of matters before we adjourn. Mr. Tieger, now are you in a position to give the position of the OTP as regards the request to append translation report to Exhibit 976.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Of course, we have no problem with the content of that CLSS filing; however, we do not consider it a proper expedient to attach it to an exhibit. It is a -- the exhibit consists of the underlying document and the translation. That translation stands as indicated by CLSS. The filing is available as requested by the Court for reference by the parties at any point and may well be referenced and by either party. But I don't think we should embark on a new approach. So for that reason we don't agree with the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the Chamber's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having examined the CLSS's memorandum as well as the parties' submissions, the Chamber notes that the B/C/S original is clear that the object of the verb "to force" is "the enemy" due to the grammatical construction. The Chamber does not find that the English translation is clear in that respect in that it leaves open the possibility that both "the enemy" and "the Muslim population" would be the object of the verb "to force." The Chamber, therefore, asks the CLSS to provide a revised translation of that portion of Exhibit P976 so that it reflects the B/C/S original accurately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I now have to ask whether there's any matters to be raised. Yes, Ms. West, first -- yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just some corrections for the transcript, please, before we forget them. Page 31, line 21, it should be Lolici. Page 6, line 13, it should be Fadil, not Fadir with an R. And then also - I can do this in open session - page 43, line 22, the witness said: "And then there was a man called ..." The name is not yet on it. It will be, and I would ask that it be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just two quick matters. Number one, I'd like -- it's clear that given the nature of the motion we would ask for a word extension for the filing with respect to one of the bar table submissions. I've discussed that with Mr. Robinson. He has no objection. The two such additional filings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes -- fine. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The final thing I wanted to mention was that, as the Court is aware, the parties have adopted a process in connection with the bar table submissions which involved a good deal of exchange of information before it was filed with -- with the Chamber in the hopes of making the work easier, reducing the number of submissions or at least refining any arguments about the items involved. That process has been necessarily abbreviated for the final motions we will be filing which may heighten the risk of a need for a reply once we've received the response, and I just wanted to -- to note that. And with that, I -- I thank the Court for its time at the closing portion of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I just don't want to let this opportunity to pass without thanking on behalf of Dr. Karadzic all of the people who have participated in the trial up to this point and particularly to commend Dr. Karadzic who has cross-examined almost 200 witnesses for over 741 hours during the two years that we've been doing this all by himself, which I think is a remarkable achievement. And he's still very healthy, has a tremendous amount of energy, and we're all looking forward to conducting a lot of direct examination during the next phase of the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, we have -- obviously share in the appreciation for the extraordinary efforts of everyone involved. We have tried where possible to convey that directly, but, of course, I didn't want any inference to be left that because we hadn't been heard publicly on this, we didn't share the appreciation for all of the extraordinary efforts involved. Sorry to raise it, but I didn't want to allow any misimpression. We thank all involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: sine die.
